# P31.4 (HARDEN.4): incremental restart + OSM replay readiness

Implements `docs/tickets/P31.4__incremental-restart-and-osm-replay-readiness.md` (Round 9 Wave A, manifest row
145, the last Wave-A ticket). Closes **D-P30.1-2** (incremental restarts), **D-P31.3-1** (hosted new-claim land
rate) and **D-P31.1-2** (the scheduled probe ran `:latest`). Opens **D-P31.4-1** (check the 2026-10-10 replay).
Stacked on P31.3 (`devin/p31-3-sink-identity-guard-and-batched-writes` @ `ffccd24`).

**Gate Q4 (ratified 2026-09-24):** switch `sig-sched-camreg-batch-05` to the new image only if the hosted bounded
test is green by 2026-10-08. **Applied: SWITCH.** The test was green on 2026-09-25.

## Summary

- **Per-capture flush.** `connectors.pipeline` calls `assert_claims` once per capture (P31.3's commit boundary),
  so an interruption loses at most the page in flight. A live PG run keeps only the records its fetch record
  needs and one artifact per stage. Memory is bounded by one capture: per-page peak growth is 165 B, against
  8.6 KB unbounded.
- **Restart = resume** (ADR-111 = ADR-R9-RESUME).
  - **Marks.** A new append-only sqitch change, `ingest_run_capture`, records per-target `captured` and
    `flushed` marks. Marks belong to P31.2's per-execution run.
  - **Logical run.** The key is `<source>@<last cron fire>` (the cadence window) plus the same connector
    version and code commit.
  - **Restart inside the window.** A restarted execution skips flushed targets but still counts them as seen
    (their digest and record count go into the report). Captured-but-unflushed targets are re-processed from
    the stored capture. If a stored capture no longer yields, the target is fetched again.
  - **What never skips.** A fresh window, or a logical run that has already completed.
- **GCS capture store.** Hosted captures lived on the container's disk; 0 bytes survived an execution. Every
  `scheduled-ingest` job now mounts the private restricted bucket (gcsfuse) as its OCFL capture store
  (`SIG_CAPTURE_DIR`).
- **Jobs pinned by digest, never `:latest`.**
  - `sig-ops roll-jobs` resolves the image, records every job's before/after digest, updates only the image,
    the capture store and `SIG_CODE_COMMIT`, then verifies. It refuses an unresolvable rollback, and it writes
    its record even when a roll fails part-way.
  - `lib.sh pin_image_digest` pins the digest for `scheduled-ops.sh`, `materialize.sh`, `export.sh` and
    `provision.sh`. `sig-ops deploy` plans a SHA tag deployed by digest.
  - `scheduled-ops.sh` batch timeout: 120m → 36h, to match the live jobs (ADR-107).
- **Bounded slices.** `--target-limit N` runs only the first N targets and records the run as `partial`.

- **Schema.** `+ ingest_run_capture .. ok` (additive).
- **Images** (both SHA-tagged; `:latest` stays `sha256:ebb6dab9…`):

- **Bounded OSM slice.** `camreg_osm_surveillance`, first 30 of 158 pages, job `sig-ingest-resume-test`. The
  same sequence ran on both images:

  | execution | image | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | killed | first | cancelled after 15 flushed; no completion |
  | resume | first | **14 fetches for 30 pages** (15 skipped, 1 re-processed from GCS), +0, 53.5 s |
  | fresh | first | 30 fetches, +0, 95.5 s |
  | fresh | final | 30 fetches, +0, 100 s |

  | resume | final | **15 fetches**, +0, 53.3 s |

  Every run emitted the same 220,009 records with the same 30 capture digests.
  - **Throughput:** 18.9 pages/min, 138k records/min.

## Review

A fresh-context review found 2 blockers and 6 should-fix items. All are fixed and tested, and the hosted test was
re-run on the fixed image before the final roll.

- **Blocker 1:** a bad stored capture was replayed on every restart. It is now fetched again.
- **Blocker 2:** the roll had to follow the schema. The schema was deployed first, and resume now degrades to
  "no resume" if the table is missing.
- **Should-fix items:**
  - resume is scoped to the code commit;
  - the roll record is written even when a roll fails part-way;
  - an unresolvable rollback digest is refused;
  - the capture volume and its env var are planned separately;
  - the drift record counts claims already flushed;
  - a bad cron string costs only the resume.

The run ledger lists every item.

**Validators:** `make docs-check`, `check-build-memory.sh .`, `check_backlog.py` (40/40), `build_backlog_md.py
--check`, `check_spec_src.py`, `tests/unit/test_policy_adrs.py`.

**Deviations:**
- The roll also covered the on-demand jobs, to meet "every job by digest".
- A second image was rolled, because the review fixes changed runtime behaviour.

No merge, tag or push to `main`.
